findings.description: F001 requires low-ceiling and high-ceiling renderer coverage, but the objective contract explicitly says low and medium ceilings must both be stated as incompleteness. A medium ceiling could regress into neutral or over-confident copy while the proposed low/high test matrix still passes.
findings.recommendation: Pin a renderer-unit case for medium confidence_ceiling, or parameterize the low-ceiling assertion across both low and medium values.

findings.description: F004 and F006 require confidence styling hooks, but the journey only demands at least one distinct hook in each producer state. The contract names heuristic, unresolved, and filesystem items as separate user-facing honesty signals; one surviving hook does not prove all three classes remain visible through the real shell.
findings.recommendation: Require the producer-generated journey fixture or assertions to cover heuristic import edges, unresolved edges or targets, and tier-0 filesystem nodes independently, with selectors proving each class survives shell rendering.

findings.description: F003 says the architecture_missing warning must be driven by the view-state absence marker and asserted by name, but the proposed feature does not pin the actual payload path. That leaves ambiguity where the renderer could infer absence from a missing architecture block instead of using the producer contract marker.
findings.recommendation: Name the exact build_view_state absence-marker path in the plan before implementation and require the renderer test to assert that specific field is the sole warning input.
